## Design Specificity Verdict

**Design review:** the control is generic. The swatches are a Material Design palette and the custom picker follows the standard square-and-hue-slider pattern. That's fine for a utility control, where Actual's "boring and correct" applies. The chrome uses the system properly: the `Popover` tooltip surface, `Input`, 4px radii and the `formInputBorderSelected` focus color. The one part designed for this product is the best one: every tag on the page recolors while you drag. The weak spot is the "correct" half. The picker doesn't know whether the tag text will stay readable, has no "Default" option, and ignores the dark and midnight themes.

**Automated scan:** 0 findings in `ColorPicker.tsx` and `CustomColorPicker.tsx`, plus 1 advisory finding (exit code 0):
- `design-system-color`, [ColorPreview.tsx:6](packages/component-library/src/ColorPreview.tsx#L6): `#d9d9d9` isn't in DESIGN.md.

The scan calls this a false positive, because it's the standard light-gray "no color" checkerboard. The design review flagged the same line from another angle: the checkerboard stays bright on dark themes. Both are right. Light checkerboards are the convention even in dark UIs, so this is low priority.

**Visual overlays:** none. There was no page to inject the scan's overlay into.

## Overall Impression

The live recolor-while-dragging is the right idea, and the plumbing behind it is solid. The weakness is the front door: the feature this branch adds sits behind a square that doesn't look clickable. Some deeper problems (swatch keyboard navigation, readable tag text, no default color) are older than this branch and are not regressions.

## What's Working

- **You judge the color on the real tag.** The preview runs through the shared tags cache on every change and saves only when you stop. So you see the color on every `#tag` on the page, not on a lone square, and dragging doesn't flood the database with saves.
- **The custom picker is tucked away correctly.** Swatches stay the fast path. The square and slider appear only on request, and the toggle tells screen readers whether it's open.
- **Thumbs don't jump.** Grays keep their hue even though tag colors are stored as hex.

## Priority Issues

**[P1] The custom picker can't be found** *(introduced on this branch)*
- **Why it matters:** this is the feature the branch adds, and nothing tells a sighted user the square is a button. It reads as a status display. Its only label is screen-reader text.
- **Fix:**
  - Make it a visibly labeled control: the preview square, then the text "Custom…" and a chevron that turns when open.
  - Give it a hover tint and an expanded state.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable clarify`

**[P1] Swatch keyboard focus is invisible, and the rows split into 8 lists** *(from before this branch)*
- [ColorPicker.tsx](packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.tsx) renders one react-aria swatch picker per row.
- Screen readers announce 8 lists with the same name, "Color swatches", and arrow keys stop at the end of each row.
- Swatch items set `outline: 'none'` and style only the selected state, so keyboard focus can't be seen. That fails WCAG 2.4.7 and PRODUCT.md's full-keyboard commitment.
- **Fix:**
  - Use a single swatch picker laid out as a 5-column grid. React Aria's grid layout then handles arrow keys in both directions.
  - Add a visible focus style using `theme.formInputBorderSelected`.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable harden`

**[P1, unconfirmed] Keys pressed inside the popover may reach the tag-creation row**
- React events bubble out of portals, and `TagCreationRow` closes on Escape and submits on Enter.
- Pressing Escape to close the picker may also discard the half-typed tag. Pressing Enter in the hex field may submit the tag.
- **Fix:** stop key events from propagating out of the picker's dialog. React Aria's own Escape-to-dismiss keeps working.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable harden`
- **To confirm:** create a tag, open its color picker, press Escape, and check whether the name you typed survives.

**[P2] No way back to the default color, and nothing keeps the tag readable** *(mostly older, made worse by this branch)*
- Once a tag has a color, it can't return to the theme default.
- `useTagCSS` chooses white or black text with a rough brightness rule. Several existing swatches already get white text below 4.5:1, for example `#0097A7` at about 3.4:1.
- A free-form picker makes such colors much easier to land on.
- Hex colors don't adapt to dark or midnight *(visual confirm)*.
- **Fix:**
  - Add a leading "Default" swatch that clears the color.
  - Choose text color by WCAG contrast instead of the brightness rule.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable harden`, then `/impeccable colorize`

**[P2] Too many options, and the advanced ones mixed in with the basics**
- There are 40 swatches in three color families with no spacing between the families.
- The hex field sits beside the swatches instead of inside the custom section.
- The `#` prefix is drawn in placeholder gray, about 2.15:1 contrast on white.
- **Fix:**
  - Group or trim the swatches.
  - Move the hex field into the custom section next to the square and slider.
  - Draw the `#` in normal text color.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable distill`

## Persona Red Flags

**Alex (power user)**
- Up to 8 Tab presses to reach a swatch in a later row.
- Each arrow keypress on the color square counts as a finished change, so it triggers its own save. Holding an arrow key sends a burst of saves *(needs confirming in the app)*.

**Sam (screen reader and keyboard user)**
- Swatch focus can't be seen, and 8 lists share one name.
- In dark theme the preview's focus ring is about 2.4:1, below the 3:1 required for focus indicators.
- Thumb focus is shown only by the thumb growing from 20px to 24px.
- "Hex color" and "Custom color" are hardcoded English, not translated.

**Pat (household budgeter, from PRODUCT.md)**
- "RRGGBB" means nothing to Pat.
- The square doesn't look clickable.
- There's no "go back to how it was".
- A bright pastel tag that's fine in light mode may glare in midnight *(visual confirm)*.

## Minor Observations

- The hex row is 140px wide in a 192px column, leaving a ragged gap on the right. The input is about 28px tall next to the 32px preview *(visual confirm)*.
- With the custom picker open, the popover is about 562px tall. On short screens the new section may open below the fold, so the click seems to do nothing *(visual confirm)*.
- In dark and midnight, the "RRGGBB" placeholder is the same color as typed text.
- The faint swatch edge disappears for dark swatches on the dark popover background.
- The selection ring's hardcoded black and white is a reasonable exception, since swatches can be any color.

## Questions to Consider

- Does someone coloring `#groceries` need 16.7 million colors, or would about a dozen theme-aware tones plus "Default" serve them better?
- What if the preview were the tag itself, `#groceries` drawn in the chosen colors, so the choice is about whether the tag stays readable?
- Should tag colors adapt per theme instead of being fixed hex values tuned for light mode?

---

### Issue 1

**Title:** Make tag color swatches keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly

**Description**

The tag color picker builds its 40 swatches as 8 separate react-aria swatch lists, one per row (`ColorSwatchPicker` in `packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.tsx`). As a result:
- Screen readers announce 8 lists that all have the same name, "Color swatches".
- Arrow keys stop at the end of each row, so reaching a swatch in a later row takes up to 8 Tab presses.
- Swatch items set `outline: 'none'` and style only the selected state, so keyboard focus can't be seen. That fails WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- The swatches are one swatch list laid out as a grid, and arrow keys move in all four directions across rows.
- A keyboard-focused swatch shows a visible focus indicator using theme tokens, with at least 3:1 contrast in light, dark and midnight.
- The swatch list has one meaningful accessible name.
- The `columns` and `colorset` props behave as they do today.

**Out of Scope**
- Changing which colors are in the swatch set.
- The custom color picker and the hex field.

**Open Questions**
- Should the focus ring sit outside the swatch (offset) so it doesn't clash with the black-and-white selection ring?

---

### Issue 2

**Title:** Keep Escape and Enter in the tag color picker from affecting the tag-creation row

**Description**

React keyboard events bubble out of portals. `TagCreationRow` closes on Escape and submits on Enter, so key presses inside the color picker popover may reach it. Pressing Escape to close the picker could discard the tag being typed, and pressing Enter in the hex field could submit it. The table navigator also handles Tab and Enter, which may interfere with focus inside the popover. **This hasn't been confirmed yet.**

**Acceptance Criteria**
- First confirm the bug: start creating a tag, open its color picker, press Escape, and check whether the typed tag name survives. Repeat with Enter in the hex field.
- If confirmed, Escape closes only the picker, and Enter in the hex field doesn't submit the tag.
- Tab moves focus correctly inside the open picker.
- Escape and Enter in the creation row still work when the picker is closed.

**Out of Scope**
- Changing the creation row's existing keyboard shortcuts.

**Open Questions**
- Should this be fixed once in `ColorPicker`, by stopping key propagation at the dialog, or in each parent row?

---

### Issue 3

**Title:** Add a "Default" tag color and keep tag text readable on any color

**Description**

Once a tag has a color, there's no way to return it to the theme's default tag style (`noteTagBackground`/`noteTagText`). Separately, `useTagCSS` picks white or black tag text with a rough brightness rule, so several existing swatches get white text below 4.5:1 contrast (`#0097A7` is about 3.4:1, for example). The free-form custom color picker makes such colors easier to choose.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- The picker has a "Default" option that clears the tag's color, and the tag then follows the theme's default tag colors.
- The tag's text color is chosen by WCAG contrast, so tag text is at least 4.5:1 on any background color.
- Existing tags with stored colors still render correctly.

**Out of Scope**
- Making stored tag colors adapt to each theme.
- Changing the swatch set.

**Open Questions**
- Where should "Default" go: as the first swatch, or as a separate button?
- Should custom colors adapt per theme in a later issue?

---

### Issue 4

**Title:** Simplify the tag color swatch set and fix the "#" prefix contrast

**Description**

The picker shows 40 swatches in three color families (saturated, pastel, light tint) with no visual separation, which makes the common choice slower. The hex field's fixed `#` prefix uses `formInputTextPlaceholder`, about 2.15:1 contrast on white. In dark and midnight, the "RRGGBB" placeholder is the same color as typed text.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- The swatches are either visually grouped by family or trimmed to a smaller set, decided with the team.
- The `#` prefix meets 4.5:1 contrast in all three themes.
- The placeholder looks different from typed text in all three themes.

**Out of Scope**
- Changes to the hex field's behavior (filtering, syncing, revert on blur).
- The custom color picker.

**Open Questions**
- Trim the swatches or group them? If trimming, which colors stay?

Base directory for this skill: /workspaces/actual-budget/.claude/skills/impeccable

This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at, and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again, rather than screenshotting after every tweak.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
| `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
| `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
| `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
| `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
| `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
| `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
| `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
| `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
| `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
| `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
| `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
| `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
| `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
| `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
| `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
| `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
| `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
| `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
| `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |
| `adapt [target]` | Fix | Adapt for different devices and screen sizes | [reference/adapt.md](reference/adapt.md) · native: [reference/adapt.native.md](reference/adapt.native.md) |
| `optimize [target]` | Fix | Diagnose and fix UI performance | [reference/optimize.md](reference/optimize.md) |
| `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, iterate on alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
| `generate [n] [action] [element]` | Iterate | Variants, versions, or alternatives of a named element to choose from in the live browser; no manual picking | [reference/generate.md](reference/generate.md) |

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

1	> **Additional context needed**: audience knowledge and emotional state.
2	
3	Rewrite unclear interface text so users understand what happened, what matters, and what to do next. Preserve factual meaning, product terminology, and brand voice.
4	
5	## Audit the language
6	
7	Read the entire interaction path, not isolated strings. Identify:
8	
9	- ambiguous nouns, verbs, and actions;
10	- internal jargon or assumed knowledge;
11	- vague labels, outcomes, and system states;
12	- missing consequences, recovery, or timing;
13	- inconsistent terminology and capitalization;
14	- redundant headings, intros, helper text, and confirmations;
15	- text that breaks at realistic widths or in translation;
16	- tone that ignores stress, risk, success, or urgency.
17	
18	Infer audience and task from product context and surrounding UI. Ask before changing factual claims, legal meaning, or a term that may be domain-specific.
19	
20	## Set the message hierarchy
21	
22	For each state, decide:
23	
24	1. the one fact the user needs now;
25	2. the action available next;
26	3. supporting context that changes the decision;
27	4. the appropriate tone for this moment.
28	
29	Say each idea once. If the heading already explains the state, the introduction should add new information or disappear.
30	
31	## Rewrite by function
32	
33	### Actions and navigation
34	
35	Use a specific verb and object when the outcome is not already obvious. Labels should describe what will happen, not the gesture used to trigger it. Keep the same noun and verb for the same concept throughout the product.
36	
37	For destructive actions, name the object and consequence. Prefer undo over confirmation when recovery is safe. When confirmation is necessary, name the action on both the message and button instead of using `Yes`, `No`, `OK`, or `Submit`.
38	
39	### Forms
40	
41	Use persistent labels; placeholders are examples, not labels. Put format and eligibility requirements before submission. Explain why information is requested only when it is not obvious. Required and optional treatment should be consistent.
42	
43	Validation says what needs attention and how to correct it without blaming the user. Keep related instructions near the field and announce errors accessibly.
44	
45	### Errors and permissions
46	
47	An actionable error answers:
48	
49	1. what failed;
50	2. why, when known and useful;
51	3. how to recover or what alternative remains.
52	
53	Do not expose internal codes as the primary message. Do not promise a cause or resolution the system cannot know. Treat privacy, payment, deletion, access loss, and blocked work seriously; warmth is welcome, jokes are not.
54	
55	### Loading, empty, and success states
56	
57	Loading text names the real operation and sets an honest expectation when the wait is meaningful. Show determinate progress when available; never invent progress.
58	
59	An empty state distinguishes first use, no results, filters, permissions, and failure. Explain the state and provide the next useful action.
60	
61	Success confirms the completed outcome and mentions the next consequence only when it changes what the user should do. Routine success should be brief.
62	
63	### Help and instructional text
64	
65	Helper text answers an implicit question instead of restating the control. Use progressive disclosure for uncommon detail. Link text must make sense out of context; icon-only controls need accessible names.
66	
67	## Voice, accessibility, and localization
68	
69	Voice stays consistent; tone adapts to the moment. Use plain language without flattening terminology the audience genuinely knows.
70	
71	- Write complete translatable messages rather than concatenated fragments.
72	- Keep variables and numbers structured so translators can reorder them.
73	- Allow expansion instead of abbreviating prematurely.
74	- Make alt text convey the image's information; use empty alt for decoration.
75	- Keep screen-reader names aligned with visible labels and outcomes.
76	- Do not rely on punctuation, color, or iconography to carry the message alone.
77	
78	Maintain a short terminology glossary when inconsistency spans the product. Do not vary words for literary effect in an interface.
79	
80	## Verify
81	
82	Read the flow in context and test:
83	
84	- comprehension without hidden product knowledge;
85	- actionability at errors, empty states, and decision points;
86	- factual accuracy and consistent terminology;
87	- scanability at target widths and 200% zoom;
88	- long names, localization expansion, pluralization, and dynamic values;
89	- accessible names and announced state changes;
90	- tone appropriate to consequence and emotional context.
91	
92	The final copy is as short as it can be without removing meaning or recovery.
93	
94	When the language reads cleanly, hand off to `/impeccable polish` for the final pass.
95
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Craft floor
2	
3	Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.
4	
5	## Verify
6	
7	Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.
8	
9	- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
10	- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
11	- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
12	- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
13	- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
14	- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
15	- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
16	- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
17	- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.
18	
19	## Refuse
20	
21	These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.
22	
23	Page scaffolds:
24	
25	- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
26	- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
27	- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
28	- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
29	- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.
30	
31	Surface habits:
32	
33	- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
34	- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
35	- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
36	- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
37	- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
38	- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
39	- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
40	- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
41	- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
42	- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.
43	
44	The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
45
```

import React, { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Tooltip as AriaTooltip, TooltipTrigger } from 'react-aria-components';

import { styles } from './styles';
import { View } from './View';

type TooltipProps = Partial<ComponentProps<typeof AriaTooltip>> & {
  children: ReactNode;
  content: ReactNode;
  triggerProps?: Partial<ComponentProps<typeof TooltipTrigger>>;
  disablePointerEvents?: boolean;
};

export const Tooltip = ({
  children,
  content,
  triggerProps = {},
  disablePointerEvents = false,
  ...props
}: TooltipProps) => {
  const triggerRef = useRef(null);
  const [isHovered, setIsHover] = useState(false);

  const hoverTimeoutRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(null);
  const closeTimeoutRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(null);

  const handlePointerEnter = useCallback(() => {
    if (closeTimeoutRef.current) {
      clearTimeout(closeTimeoutRef.current);
    }

    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
      setIsHover(true);
    }, triggerProps.delay ?? 300);

    hoverTimeoutRef.current = timeout;
  }, [triggerProps.delay]);

  const handlePointerLeave = useCallback(() => {
    if (hoverTimeoutRef.current) {
      clearTimeout(hoverTimeoutRef.current);
    }

    closeTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
      setIsHover(false);
    }, triggerProps.closeDelay ?? 0);
  }, [triggerProps.closeDelay]);

  // Force closing the tooltip whenever the disablement state changes
  useEffect(() => {
    setIsHover(false);
  }, [triggerProps.isDisabled]);

  return (
    <View
      style={{ minHeight: 'auto', flexShrink: 0, maxWidth: '100%' }}
      ref={triggerRef}
      onMouseEnter={handlePointerEnter}
      onMouseLeave={handlePointerLeave}
    >
      <TooltipTrigger
        isOpen={isHovered && !triggerProps.isDisabled}
        {...triggerProps}
      >
        {children}

        <AriaTooltip
          triggerRef={triggerRef}
          style={{
            ...styles.tooltip,
            ...(disablePointerEvents && { pointerEvents: 'none' }),
          }}
          {...props}
        >
          {content}
        </AriaTooltip>
      </TooltipTrigger>
    </View>
  );
};
```

**What changed** (only in [ColorPicker.tsx](packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.tsx)):

- **Chevron:** it flips to point up while the picker is open. The 150ms rotation is turned off for people who've asked their system to reduce motion.
- **States:**

  - While the picker is open, the border turns the accent purple, the same color the hex field's border turns when focused.
  - The keyboard focus ring is unchanged.
- **Wording:** hovering shows a tooltip, "Pick a custom color". The screen-reader label went from "Custom color" to the same "Pick a custom color", so what people see and hear matches. I updated the tests to use the new name.
- **Contrast:** I checked my colors in all three themes and changed two that failed. The chevron now uses `formInputText`, which is at least 8.8:1 in every theme. The hover tint is `buttonBareBackgroundHover`, because the first token I picked showed no hover change in light and dropped to 2.98:1 in midnight.

- **The picker opens when you click the color preview box:** yes. The preview is still there, inside the button, and clicking it opens the picker.
- **Tags update live:** yes, unchanged.
- **The hex field still works and stays in sync:** yes. I didn't touch the input, its `#`, its placeholder or its behavior, as the issue's out-of-scope note requires. The preview still follows what you type, including the checkerboard for incomplete values.

**Decisions for you:**
- **The preview got smaller, from 32px to 20px.** That's how it fits inside a button the height of the input. It does change how PR #136's preview looks, so check it's acceptable.

Base directory for this skill: /workspaces/actual-budget/.claude/skills/impeccable

This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at, and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again, rather than screenshotting after every tweak.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

````text
1	Designs that only work with perfect data aren't production-ready. Harden the interface against the inputs, errors, languages, and network conditions that real users will throw at it.
2	
3	## Assess Hardening Needs
4	
5	Identify weaknesses and edge cases:
6	
7	1. **Test with extreme inputs**:
8	   - Very long text (names, descriptions, titles)
9	   - Very short text (empty, single character)
10	   - Special characters (emoji, RTL text, accents)
11	   - Large numbers (millions, billions)
12	   - Many items (1000+ list items, 50+ options)
13	   - No data (empty states)
14	
15	2. **Test error scenarios**:
16	   - Network failures (offline, slow, timeout)
17	   - API errors (400, 401, 403, 404, 500)
18	   - Validation errors
19	   - Permission errors
20	   - Rate limiting
21	   - Concurrent operations
22	
23	3. **Test internationalization**:
24	   - Long translations (German is often 30% longer than English)
25	   - RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew)
26	   - Character sets (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, emoji)
27	   - Date/time formats
28	   - Number formats (1,000 vs 1.000)
29	   - Currency symbols
30	
31	Designs that only work with perfect data aren't production-ready.
32	
33	## Hardening Dimensions
34	
35	Systematically improve resilience:
36	
37	### Text Overflow & Wrapping
38	
39	**Long text handling**:
40	```css
41	/* Single line with ellipsis */
42	.truncate {
43	  overflow: hidden;
44	  text-overflow: ellipsis;
45	  white-space: nowrap;
46	}
47	
48	/* Multi-line with clamp */
49	.line-clamp {
50	  display: -webkit-box;
51	  -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
52	  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
53	  overflow: hidden;
54	}
55	
56	/* Allow wrapping */
57	.wrap {
58	  word-wrap: break-word;
59	  overflow-wrap: break-word;
60	  hyphens: auto;
61	}
62	```
63	
64	**Flex/Grid overflow**:
65	```css
66	/* Prevent flex items from overflowing */
67	.flex-item {
68	  min-width: 0; /* Allow shrinking below content size */
69	  overflow: hidden;
70	}
71	
72	/* Prevent grid items from overflowing */
73	.grid-item {
74	  min-width: 0;
75	  min-height: 0;
76	}
77	```
78	
79	**Responsive text sizing**:
80	- Use `clamp()` for fluid typography
81	- Set minimum readable sizes (16px body on mobile, the same floor the typography guidance sets; 14px only for genuinely secondary text. iOS Safari force-zooms focused inputs under 16px, which breaks form layouts)
82	- Test text scaling (zoom to 200%)
83	- Ensure containers expand with text
84	
85	### Internationalization (i18n)
86	
87	**Text expansion**:
88	- Add 30-40% space budget for translations
89	- Use flexbox/grid that adapts to content
90	- Test with longest language (usually German)
91	- Avoid fixed widths on text containers
92	
93	```jsx
94	// ❌ Bad: Assumes short English text
95	<button className="w-24">Submit</button>
96	
97	// ✅ Good: Adapts to content
98	<button className="px-4 py-2">Submit</button>
99	```
100	
101	**RTL (Right-to-Left) support**:
102	```css
103	/* Use logical properties */
104	margin-inline-start: 1rem; /* Not margin-left */
105	padding-inline: 1rem; /* Not padding-left/right */
106	border-inline-end: 1px solid; /* Not border-right */
107	
108	/* Or use dir attribute */
109	[dir="rtl"] .arrow { transform: scaleX(-1); }
110	```
111	
112	**Arabic-script specifics** (Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Pashto, Kurdish):
113	- Preserve Zero-Width Non-Joiner (U+200C). Persian and Kurdish use ZWNJ between compound-word parts to break cursive joining while keeping the word together. A filter or sanitizer that strips it changes meaning. Never normalize it away.
114	- Handle Yeh and Kaf variants. Persian uses ی (U+06CC) and ک (U+06A9), while Arabic uses ي (U+064A) and ك (U+0643). Preserve the original form in storage. For search and validation, treat the corresponding letters as equivalent so that Arabic-keyboard input matches Persian text. Rejecting one variant locks out users whose keyboard sends the other.
115	- Support locale-aware digits. Persian (`fa-IR`) and Arabic locales use Eastern Arabic-Indic numerals (۰-۹ and ٠-٩). Use `Intl.NumberFormat` with the correct locale rather than hardcoding Western digits.
116	
117	```javascript
118	// ✅ Locale-aware digit formatting
119	new Intl.NumberFormat('fa-IR').format(1234); // ۱٬۲۳۴
120	new Intl.NumberFormat('ar-SA').format(1234); // ١٬٢٣٤
121	```
122	
123	- Respect calendar systems. Persian users expect the Solar Hijri (Jalali) calendar; many Arabic-speaking users expect the Hijri (Islamic) calendar. Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the appropriate locale or calendar parameter.
124	
125	```javascript
126	// ✅ Locale-appropriate calendar
127	new Intl.DateTimeFormat('fa-IR').format(new Date());
128	new Intl.DateTimeFormat('ar-SA-u-ca-islamic').format(new Date());
129	```
130	
131	**Character set support**:
132	- Use UTF-8 encoding everywhere
133	- Test with Chinese/Japanese/Korean (CJK) characters
134	- Test with emoji (they can be 2-4 bytes)
135	- Handle different scripts (Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, etc.)
136	
137	**Date/Time formatting**:
138	```javascript
139	// ✅ Use Intl API for proper formatting
140	new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US').format(date); // 1/15/2024
141	new Intl.DateTimeFormat('de-DE').format(date); // 15.1.2024
142	
143	new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { 
144	  style: 'currency', 
145	  currency: 'USD' 
146	}).format(1234.56); // $1,234.56
147	```
148	
149	**Pluralization**:
150	```javascript
151	// ❌ Bad: Assumes English pluralization
152	`${count} item${count !== 1 ? 's' : ''}`
153	
154	// ✅ Good: Use proper i18n library
155	t('items', { count }) // Handles complex plural rules
156	```
157	
158	### Error Handling
159	
160	**Network errors**:
161	- Show clear error messages
162	- Provide retry button
163	- Explain what happened
164	- Offer offline mode (if applicable)
165	- Handle timeout scenarios
166	
167	```jsx
168	// Error states with recovery
169	{error && (
170	  <ErrorMessage>
171	    <p>Failed to load data. {error.message}</p>
172	    <button onClick={retry}>Try again</button>
173	  </ErrorMessage>
174	)}
175	```
176	
177	**Form validation errors**:
178	- Inline errors near fields
179	- Clear, specific messages
180	- Suggest corrections
181	- Don't block submission unnecessarily
182	- Preserve user input on error
183	
184	**API errors**:
185	- Handle each status code appropriately
186	  - 400: Show validation errors
187	  - 401: Redirect to login
188	  - 403: Show permission error
189	  - 404: Show not found state
190	  - 429: Show rate limit message
191	  - 500: Show generic error, offer support
192	
193	**Graceful degradation**:
194	- Core functionality works without JavaScript
195	- Images have alt text
196	- Progressive enhancement
197	- Fallbacks for unsupported features
198	
199	### Edge Cases & Boundary Conditions
200	
201	**Empty states**:
202	- No items in list
203	- No search results
204	- No notifications
205	- No data to display
206	- Provide clear next action
207	
208	**Loading states**:
209	- Initial load
210	- Pagination load
211	- Refresh
212	- Show what's loading ("Loading your projects...")
213	- Time estimates for long operations
214	
215	**Large datasets**:
216	- Pagination or virtual scrolling
217	- Search/filter capabilities
218	- Performance optimization
219	- Don't load all 10,000 items at once
220	
221	**Concurrent operations**:
222	- Prevent double-submission (disable button while loading)
223	- Handle race conditions
224	- Optimistic updates with rollback
225	- Conflict resolution
226	
227	**Interrupted gestures** (custom sliders, drag surfaces, scrollable control strips):
228	- A second finger or pointer lands mid-drag: the first drag keeps its pointer or ends cleanly, never jumps to the new one
229	- The browser cancels the gesture to scroll (`pointercancel`), capture is lost (`lostpointercapture`), the pointer is released outside the control, or the window loses focus (`blur`) mid-drag: clear the dragging state and release capture
230	- After each of these, the next tap or drag works without a reload
231	
232	**Permission states**:
233	- No permission to view
234	- No permission to edit
235	- Read-only mode
236	- Clear explanation of why
237	
238	**Browser compatibility**:
239	- Polyfills for modern features
240	- Fallbacks for unsupported CSS
241	- Feature detection (not browser detection)
242	- Test in target browsers
243	
244	### Input Validation & Sanitization
245	
246	**Client-side validation**:
247	- Required fields
248	- Format validation (email, phone, URL)
249	- Length limits
250	- Pattern matching
251	- Custom validation rules
252	
253	**Server-side validation** (always):
254	- Never trust client-side only
255	- Validate and sanitize all inputs
256	- Protect against injection attacks
257	- Rate limiting
258	
259	**Constraint handling**:
260	```html
261	<!-- Set clear constraints -->
262	<input 
263	  type="text"
264	  maxlength="100"
265	  pattern="[A-Za-z0-9]+"
266	  required
267	  aria-describedby="username-hint"
268	/>
269	<small id="username-hint">
270	  Letters and numbers only, up to 100 characters
271	</small>
272	```
273	
274	### Accessibility Resilience
275	
276	**Keyboard navigation**:
277	- All functionality accessible via keyboard
278	- Logical tab order
279	- Focus management in modals
280	- Skip links for long content
281	
282	**Screen reader support**:
283	- Proper ARIA labels
284	- Announce dynamic changes (live regions)
285	- Descriptive alt text
286	- Semantic HTML
287	
288	**High contrast mode**:
289	- Test in Windows high contrast mode
290	- Don't rely only on color
291	- Provide alternative visual cues
292	
293	### Performance Resilience
294	
295	**Slow connections**:
296	- Progressive image loading
297	- Skeleton screens
298	- Optimistic UI updates
299	- Offline support (service workers)
300	
301	**Memory leaks**:
302	- Clean up event listeners
303	- Cancel subscriptions
304	- Clear timers/intervals
305	- Abort pending requests on unmount
306	
307	**Throttling & Debouncing**:
308	```javascript
309	// Debounce search input
310	const debouncedSearch = debounce(handleSearch, 300);
311	
312	// Throttle scroll handler
313	const throttledScroll = throttle(handleScroll, 100);
314	```
315	
316	## Testing Strategies
317	
318	**Manual testing**:
319	- Test with extreme data (very long, very short, empty)
320	- Test in different languages
321	- Test offline
322	- Test slow connection (throttle to 3G)
323	- Test with screen reader
324	- Test keyboard-only navigation
325	- Test on old browsers
326	
327	**Automated testing**:
328	- Unit tests for edge cases
329	- Integration tests for error scenarios
330	- E2E tests for critical paths
331	- A behavioral regression for each confirmed gesture fix, when the project's test runner can drive input
332	- Visual regression tests
333	- Accessibility tests (axe, WAVE)
334	
335	**Avoid**:
336	- Assume perfect input (validate everything)
337	- Ignore internationalization (design for global)
338	- Leave error messages generic ("Error occurred")
339	- Forget offline scenarios
340	- Trust client-side validation alone
341	- Use fixed widths for text
342	- Assume English-length text
343	- Block entire interface when one component errors
344	
345	## Verify Hardening
346	
347	Test thoroughly with edge cases:
348	
349	- **Long text**: Try names with 100+ characters
350	- **Emoji**: Use emoji in all text fields
351	- **RTL**: Test with Arabic or Hebrew
352	- **CJK**: Test with Chinese/Japanese/Korean
353	- **Network issues**: Disable internet, throttle connection
354	- **Large datasets**: Test with 1000+ items
355	- **Concurrent actions**: Click submit 10 times rapidly
356	- **Interrupted gestures**: Add a second finger mid-drag, scroll across the control, release outside it, switch windows mid-drag; then drag again
357	- **Errors**: Force API errors, test all error states
358	- **Empty**: Remove all data, test empty states
359	
360	For gestures, say what produced the evidence (emulated viewport, synthesized touch, which engine, physical device) and name what stayed untested.
361	
362	When edge cases are covered, hand off to `/impeccable polish` for the final pass.
363
````

import { useEffect, useEffectEvent, useRef } from 'react';
import type { FocusEvent } from 'react';
import {
  ColorArea,
  ColorSlider,
  ColorThumb,
  SliderTrack,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import type { Color } from 'react-aria-components';

import { css } from '@emotion/css';

import { View } from './View';

// The thumb sits on arbitrary colors, so it pairs a white ring with a dark one
// instead of using theme tokens: one of the two always stands out
const thumbClassName = css({
  width: 20,
  height: 20,
  borderRadius: '50%',
  boxSizing: 'border-box',
  border: '2px solid white',
  boxShadow: '0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6), inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)',
  forcedColorAdjust: 'none',
  '&[data-focus-visible]': {
    width: 24,
    height: 24,
    border: '3px solid white',
    boxShadow:
      '0 0 0 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85), inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)',
  },
});

type CustomColorPickerProps = {
  id?: string;
  onChangeEnd?: (color: Color) => void;
};

// Reads and writes the surrounding ColorPicker's state, so it stays in sync
// with the swatches and the hex field without any wiring of its own
export function CustomColorPicker({ id, onChangeEnd }: CustomColorPickerProps) {
  // Every keyboard step counts as a finished change, so holding an arrow key
  // would settle (and save) on each repeat; hold those until the key is up
  const isKeyDown = useRef(false);
  const pendingColor = useRef<Color | null>(null);

  const flushPending = useEffectEvent(() => {
    const color = pendingColor.current;
    pendingColor.current = null;
    if (color) {
      onChangeEnd?.(color);
    }
  });

  // Closing the popover mid-keypress unmounts this before the key is released
  useEffect(() => () => flushPending(), []);

  const handleChangeEnd = (color: Color) => {
    if (isKeyDown.current) {
      pendingColor.current = color;
    } else {
      onChangeEnd?.(color);
    }
  };

  const releaseKey = () => {
    isKeyDown.current = false;
    flushPending();
  };

  return (
    <View
      id={id}
      style={{ gap: 8 }}
      onKeyDownCapture={() => {
        isKeyDown.current = true;
      }}
      onKeyUpCapture={releaseKey}
      onBlur={(e: FocusEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
        // The key may be released after focus has moved elsewhere
        if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget)) {
          releaseKey();
        }
      }}
    >
      <ColorArea
        colorSpace="hsb"
        xChannel="saturation"
        yChannel="brightness"
        onChangeEnd={handleChangeEnd}
        style={{
          width: '100%',
          height: 140,
          borderRadius: 4,
          flexShrink: 0,
          forcedColorAdjust: 'none',
        }}
      >
        <ColorThumb className={thumbClassName} />
      </ColorArea>
      <ColorSlider colorSpace="hsb" channel="hue" onChangeEnd={handleChangeEnd}>
        <SliderTrack
          style={{ height: 24, borderRadius: 4, forcedColorAdjust: 'none' }}
        >
          <ColorThumb className={thumbClassName} style={{ top: '50%' }} />
        </SliderTrack>
      </ColorSlider>
    </View>
  );
}

```

I fixed both issues from the critique. Formatting, lint, typecheck and the design scan pass. The tests, including a new one, are written but still can't run here because vitest can't start, and I haven't watched any of this in a browser.

**1. Holding an arrow key no longer saves on every repeat**
- **Confirmed in react-aria's code:** every keyboard step counts as a finished change, and with option A each one triggered a database save and a sync message. That's about 30 a second while a key is held.
- **Fix** in [CustomColorPicker.tsx](packages/component-library/src/CustomColorPicker.tsx): while a key is down inside the square or hue slider, the picker remembers the latest color instead of saving it. When the key is released, it saves once. Tags still recolor live the whole time, since that comes from `onChange`, which I didn't touch.
- **Edge cases covered:**
  - **Focus leaves before the key is released** (for example Tab): the save happens when focus leaves the picker.
  - **The popover closes while a key is held:** the save happens when the picker closes.
  - **Mouse and touch drags:** they don't hold a key, so they still save once when the drag ends.
- **New test:** three key presses with the key held give three live updates and no save, then exactly one save of the final color on release.

**2. The thumb's focus ring stands out on any color**
- Before, keyboard focus only made the thumb a little bigger. Now a focused thumb also gets a thicker white ring and a darker outer ring.
- The thumb sits on whatever color you've picked, so theme colors can't be relied on. Pairing a white ring with a dark one means one of them always contrasts. A code comment explains why white and black are hardcoded.
- The color square and slider are now set not to be recolored by Windows high-contrast mode, matching the swatches. Without that, high-contrast mode would wash out the gradients and hide the thumb outlines.

**Acceptance criteria:** all three still hold. The picker opens from the preview, tags update live (keyboard drags too, since only the save waits), and the hex field still syncs. I didn't touch the hex input.

**Not checked:**
- **Interrupted gestures:** a second finger, the browser cancelling a drag to scroll, or releasing outside the control. React-aria handles all of these, but I haven't tested them on a real device.
- **Screen reader and RTL:** react-aria supplies translated labels and right-to-left behavior for the square and slider. I haven't heard them with a screen reader or seen them in an RTL language.
- **The dark-theme focus ring** on the preview button (2.39:1) is unchanged. It uses the same `formInputBorderSelected` token as every input's focus border, so it's an app-wide question for a separate issue.

**To check by hand:**
- In the tag editor, open the picker, tab to the hue slider and hold an arrow key. The tag should recolor smoothly, with one save when you let go.
- Confirm the focused thumb is easy to see on light, dark and saturated colors.

The last step on the list is `/impeccable polish packages/component-library/src/ColorPicker.tsx`.

Base directory for this skill: /workspaces/actual-budget/.claude/skills/impeccable

This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at, and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again, rather than screenshotting after every tweak.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

## Commands

| Command | Category | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
| `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
| `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
| `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
| `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |

| `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
| `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |

| `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |

| `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, iterate on alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
| `generate [n] [action] [element]` | Iterate | Variants, versions, or alternatives of a named element to choose from in the live browser; no manual picking | [reference/generate.md](reference/generate.md) |

Routing:

- **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
- **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
- **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
- **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
- `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.

After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.

**Pin / Unpin:** `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.

**Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.

**Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.

**Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.

```typescript
import { useContext, useEffect, useEffectEvent, useRef } from 'react';
import type { FocusEvent, KeyboardEvent } from 'react';
import {
  ColorArea,
  ColorPickerStateContext,
  ColorSlider,
  ColorThumb,
  SliderTrack,
  useLocale,
} from 'react-aria-components';
import type { Color, ColorChannel } from 'react-aria-components';

import { css } from '@emotion/css';

import { View } from './View';

// The thumb sits on arbitrary colors, so it pairs a white ring with a dark one
// instead of using theme tokens: one of the two always stands out
const thumbClassName = css({
  width: 20,
  height: 20,
  borderRadius: '50%',
  boxSizing: 'border-box',
  border: '2px solid white',
  boxShadow: '0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6), inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)',
  forcedColorAdjust: 'none',
  '&[data-focus-visible]': {
    width: 24,
    height: 24,
    border: '3px solid white',
    boxShadow:
      '0 0 0 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85), inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)',
  },
});

type KeyAxes = {
  horizontal: ColorChannel;
  vertical: ColorChannel;
  maxStep: number;
};

const AREA_AXES: KeyAxes = {
  horizontal: 'saturation',
  vertical: 'brightness',
  maxStep: 4,
};
const HUE_AXES: KeyAxes = { horizontal: 'hue', vertical: 'hue', maxStep: 10 };

type CustomColorPickerProps = {
  id?: string;
  onChangeEnd?: (color: Color) => void;
};

// Reads and writes the surrounding ColorPicker's state, so it stays in sync
// with the swatches and the hex field without any wiring of its own
export function CustomColorPicker({ id, onChangeEnd }: CustomColorPickerProps) {
  const state = useContext(ColorPickerStateContext);
  const { direction } = useLocale();

  // Every keyboard step counts as a finished change, so holding an arrow key
  // would settle (and save) on each repeat; hold those until the key is up
  const isKeyDown = useRef(false);
  const pendingColor = useRef<Color | null>(null);
  const repeatCount = useRef(0);

  const flushPending = useEffectEvent(() => {
    const color = pendingColor.current;
    pendingColor.current = null;
    if (color) {
      onChangeEnd?.(color);
    }
  });

  // Closing the popover mid-keypress unmounts this before the key is released
  useEffect(() => () => flushPending(), []);

  // The popover caps its height to the viewport, so on short screens this
  // could open below the fold and look like the toggle did nothing
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    containerRef.current?.scrollIntoView?.({ block: 'nearest' });
  }, []);

  const handleChangeEnd = (color: Color) => {
    if (isKeyDown.current) {
      pendingColor.current = color;
    } else {
      onChangeEnd?.(color);
    }
  };

  const releaseKey = () => {
    isKeyDown.current = false;
    repeatCount.current = 0;
    flushPending();
  };

  // React Aria moves one unit per key repeat (1° of hue, 1% of saturation or
  // brightness), so a held arrow key crawls. A tap still moves one unit, but
  // repeats take over and grow the step the longer the key is held.
  const accelerateHeldArrow = (
    e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>,
    { horizontal, vertical, maxStep }: KeyAxes,
  ) => {
    const isHorizontal = e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowRight';
    const isArrow = isHorizontal || e.key === 'ArrowUp' || e.key === 'ArrowDown';
    // Shift already makes React Aria take its larger page steps
    if (!state || !e.repeat || !isArrow || e.shiftKey) {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();

    repeatCount.current += 1;
    const step = Math.min(1 + Math.floor(repeatCount.current / 3), maxStep);
    const forwardKey = direction === 'rtl' ? 'ArrowLeft' : 'ArrowRight';
    const sign = e.key === 'ArrowUp' || e.key === forwardKey ? 1 : -1;

    const channel = isHorizontal ? horizontal : vertical;
    const color = state.color.toFormat('hsb');
    const { minValue, maxValue } = color.getChannelRange(channel);
    const value = Math.min(
      maxValue,
      Math.max(minValue, color.getChannelValue(channel) + sign * step),
    );
    const next = color.withChannelValue(channel, value);

    state.setColor(next);
    pendingColor.current = next;
  };

  return (
    <View
      id={id}
      innerRef={containerRef}
      style={{ gap: 8, marginTop: 4 }}
      onKeyDownCapture={() => {
        isKeyDown.current = true;
      }}
      onKeyUpCapture={releaseKey}
      onBlur={(e: FocusEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
        // The key may be released after focus has moved elsewhere
        if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget)) {
          releaseKey();
        }
      }}
    >
      <View onKeyDownCapture={e => accelerateHeldArrow(e, AREA_AXES)}>
        <ColorArea
          colorSpace="hsb"
          xChannel="saturation"
          yChannel="brightness"
          onChangeEnd={handleChangeEnd}
          style={{
            width: '100%',
            height: 140,
            borderRadius: 4,
            flexShrink: 0,
            forcedColorAdjust: 'none',
          }}
        >
          <ColorThumb className={thumbClassName} />
        </ColorArea>
      </View>
      <View onKeyDownCapture={e => accelerateHeldArrow(e, HUE_AXES)}>
        <ColorSlider
          colorSpace="hsb"
          channel="hue"
          onChangeEnd={handleChangeEnd}
        >
          <SliderTrack
            style={{ height: 24, borderRadius: 4, forcedColorAdjust: 'none' }}
          >
            <ColorThumb className={thumbClassName} style={{ top: '50%' }} />
          </SliderTrack>
        </ColorSlider>
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

```
